newsitem.title: GERMANY: Star Alliance to seek close cargo links -Lufthansa.
newsitem.headline: Star Alliance to seek close cargo links -Lufthansa.

text.p: The newly-launched Star Alliance will seek to develop closer cargo links between member airlines, a senior Lufthansa manager said on Wednesday.
Wilhelm Althen, chairman of Lufthansa Cargo AG (LCAG), told Reuters that the Star Alliance could help Lufthansa develop its global freight network.
But the alliance could not replace long-standing, successful air cargo joint ventures with other carriers which were not part of the new passenger-orientated grouping, he stressed.
In an interview at the Star Alliance launch in Frankfurt, Althen said: "We have agreed that freight will be discussed in the alliance. We will try with our partners to develop synergy effects.
"We feel that freight is part of the Star Alliance. We will not now establish a Moon Alliance (for freight)," he added.
LCAG sales and marketing board member Stefan Lauer would represent Lufthansa Cargo in the Star Alliance steering committee, Althen said.
But the Star Alliance concept of seamless travel with selected partners via hubs could not be transferred directly into the cargo business, he pointed out.
"For our clients it is important that the freight is there when we promise it and the airline which flies it is not so important. The important thing is we fly directly to every point in the world."
Lufthansa Cargo, the world's largest international air cargo carrier, embarked on building a global network in 1994 to meet the needs of companies producing and distributing worldwide.

"Our global clients want a global network and we cannot do that alone in cargo, so we need partners. We have been working on a global network for three years and will continue to do that," Althen said.
Lufthansa now has functioning cargo agreements with Star Alliance members Thai Airways International, Scandinavian Airline System and future member Varig.
A global sales and marketing deal was agreed with United Airlines last autumn and closer co-operation was now starting with Air Canada, Althen said.
But for Europe-Asia traffic, LCAG had had agreements with Japan Air Lines, Cathay Pacific, Korean Airlines and Singapore Airlines for more than 10 years, Althen stressed.
"Transpacific is a gap for us but United now flies there with freighters and is coming into our network," Althen added.

Lufthansa serves the North American market virtually alone with regular freighter flights, Europe-South America is covered with Varig, while a partnership with South African Airways (SAA.CN) targeted southern Africa.
